notes.text: You just opened a story. This panel is where longer detail lives — notes, and (on a laptop instance) the Claude/Codex work sessions launched for this card. A story title is one line of Markdown; a note is the room to explain it. Next: close this, then drag the '👉 Try it' card in Todo over to Doing.

Drag-and-drop writes the move straight back to the Markdown lane files — no database. Because storage is plain text, a human dragging a card and an agent POSTing to /api/sync are editing the exact same source of truth.

The server owns ID generation: an agent POSTs a story with just text + status, and /api/sync assigns the stable t:xxxxxxx id and prepends it to the right lane file. That's why an agent never has to invent an id — it reads the receipt to learn it.

In progress: moves carry expected_text as an optimistic lock. If the stored line changed since the agent last read it, the sync receipt reports a skip instead of silently overwriting, and the agent re-fetches and retries. Prevents a human drag and an agent move from clobbering each other.
